system.name: Rassam
system.description: An open, human-owned architecture contract for agent-built software: a local-first canvas, an isomorphic rules engine, a CLI, an MCP server and a CI gate. Rassam dogfoods its own contract.

components.name: Web shell
components.intent: Next.js pages that mount the Studio and the settings page. Thin wiring only: no business logic, no data access. Logic belongs in hooks and libraries so it can be tested.

components.name: API routes
components.intent: Server route handlers. Every request body is untrusted and validated with zod; every route goes through request-security (rate limits, origin checks). Credentials stay here and never appear in responses or exports.

components.name: UI primitives
components.intent: The design system: tokens-driven buttons, sheets, popovers, pills and status glyphs. Status is never shown by colour alone; everything is keyboard reachable. Depends on nothing else in the app.

components.name: Studio
components.intent: The first screen and the main product: is the project on track? Five persistent elements only (source pill, health pill, canvas, intent bar, zoom cluster). People say what they want changed; every change is previewed on the canvas before it is applied and can be undone. Manual forms exist but stay behind progressive disclosure.

components.name: Blueprint UI
components.intent: Where humans author the contract and rule on exceptions: the blueprint canvas, the ranked attention list, rule and intent editors, and the reach view. It must keep human attention scarce: a short ranked list first, evidence links instead of persuasive prose.

components.name: State hooks
components.intent: Client state and lifecycles for blueprint sessions: loading a source, drafts, proposals, history and live status. Hooks own state; components render it.

components.name: Blueprint client
components.intent: Browser-side host for the engine: loads a blueprint for a GitHub project through the API, or reads and writes a local folder through the File System Access API so edits land in the user's repository. Heavy analysis runs in a Web Worker so large repositories do not freeze the canvas.

components.name: Settings store
components.intent: Browser-side persistence of the chosen provider, model and generation settings in localStorage. It stores choices and cached availability, never credentials.

components.name: Blueprint intent
components.intent: Server-side helpers for "tell Rassam what to change": builds the model prompt (edit operation catalogue, selector grammar, a compact blueprint digest inside data delimiters) and reads the answer (tolerant JSON extraction, schema validation, dry run). Pure text in, typed edits out: it never calls a provider and never sees credentials.

components.name: GitHub gateway
components.intent: The only code that talks to GitHub and holds GITHUB_TOKEN. Resolves public repositories to a pinned commit and binds repository identity and commit with signed source grants so clients cannot request content they were not granted.

components.name: Server platform
components.intent: Cross-cutting server concerns: rate limiting, origin and deployment checks, request parsing, the error envelope and privacy-preserving telemetry.

components.name: LLM providers
components.intent: Adapters over model providers behind one interface, and the resolver that turns a requested provider and model into exactly that configured runtime, with no silent fallback. The only code that reads provider API keys.

components.name: Shared library
components.intent: Runtime-neutral code shared by browser and server: zod request contracts and limits, version constants and small utilities. Nothing here may need Node or server credentials.

components.name: Blueprint engine
components.intent: The isomorphic heart of Rassam: blueprint format, import graph, rules, gate, reach analysis and reports. It runs unchanged in the CLI, the MCP server, CI and the browser, so it must not depend on Node, the DOM, React, Next or any other part of the app. Same inputs must always give the same findings and fingerprints.

components.name: CLI and MCP server
components.intent: The Node host: `rassam` commands, git and GitHub Actions integration, and the dual-era MCP server agents call before acting. Agent proposals and escalations are written to files for humans; the CLI never edits the blueprint on an agent's behalf.

components.name: Build tooling
components.intent: Build, lint, test, bundling and release configuration: the CLI bundle consumed by the GitHub Action, and the npm package (packages/rassam) that ships the same bundle and nothing else. The package version must equal ENGINE_VERSION, and it is published only by the release workflow on a version tag.

components.name: Tests
components.intent: Unit, integration and browser tests. Tests may depend on anything; nothing may depend on tests.

components.name: Gate benchmark
components.intent: Labeled scenarios (documented agent reward hacks, architecture violations, reach problems and legitimate changes) that measure the gate's recall and false positives. Results are published, including misses.

components.name: GitHub API
components.intent: Public repository trees and blobs, and PR comments from the GitHub Action.

components.name: Model provider APIs
components.intent: DeepSeek, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Ollama endpoints, called only through llm-providers.

dependencies.reason: The blueprint route reuses the pure layout parser.
The panel and canvas consume the useBlueprint session.
The runtime resolver reports unsupported or unconfigured selections through the shared error envelope.
Type-only: provider ids in saved model settings.
Preview and maintenance scripts reuse the CLI's working-tree loader.
Type-only: provider ids on the settings page.

rules.reason: The engine runs in the CLI, the MCP server, CI and the browser. Host APIs belong in src/cli or src/lib/blueprint-client; app code must never leak into it.
The CLI is bundled into a single dependency-free file for the GitHub Action; it may use only the engine, Node built-ins and zod.
Browser bundles must never include server modules that read credentials or call providers. Type-only imports are fine.
One place holds the GitHub credential; the CLI reads the Actions token only to post the sticky PR comment.
Provider keys are read only by the adapters that call providers.
Signing and rate-limit secrets stay in the server platform and the routes that check readiness.
Shared code is bundled into the browser and the server alike, so it must not pull in Node built-ins or server-only modules.
Production code must never depend on test code.
Cycles erase the direction of dependency, so no component can change safely in isolation.
Rate limits, signed source grants, origin checks and security headers. Changes here need a human security review.

invariants.statement: Under the default policy, a change that skips, focuses, deletes or guts tests, lowers a coverage threshold or forces a success exit fails until a human applies the approval label, and no legitimate change in the benchmark's negatives fails.

provenance.note: Added with the require-approval policy; a human should verify it.

invariants.statement: A change is judged by the base branch's blueprint; it cannot relax the contract it is checked against, and weakening edits are errors until a human approves them.
The engine is deterministic: the same snapshot and blueprint always produce the same findings, order and fingerprints.
AI output never mutates the blueprint directly; it becomes a validated, dry-run proposal that a human previews and applies, and agent proposals from the CLI are written to files for review.
Provider keys and the GitHub token never reach the browser, reports or logs; secrets in reports are always redacted.

decisions.title: Pivot from repository diagrams to architecture contracts
decisions.context: Repository-to-diagram is now free from Google Code Wiki, DeepWiki, Codemaps and GitDiagram. Agents author a large and growing share of merged code while review time has risen sharply; the scarce human contributions are intent, enforcement and sign-off.
decisions.decision: Rassam becomes an open, vendor-neutral, human-owned architecture contract (.rassam/blueprint.json) that agents read over MCP, a CI gate enforces, and humans author and sign on a canvas.
decisions.consequences: The map canvas becomes secondary. Investment moves to the engine, the gate, the MCP server and authoring UX. Success is measured by human-authored invariants and violations caught, not diagrams drawn.
links: reports/Rassam pivot for the AGI era.md

decisions.title: Judge every change by the base blueprint
decisions.context: Documented reward hacks by coding agents attack the checks themselves. If a pull request could edit the rules it is judged by, an agent could relax its own contract.
decisions.decision: The gate evaluates a change against the blueprint at the merge-base. Contract edits are diffed semantically; weakening edits are errors until a human applies the approval label. Invariant commands run only from the base blueprint.
decisions.consequences: Introducing or tightening rules takes effect after merge. Teams must approve contract changes explicitly.

decisions.title: Static analysis is the only source of edges
decisions.context: LLMs are weakest at recovering relationships between modules, and LLM-written context files did not improve agent outcomes while adding cost.
decisions.decision: Dependencies come from deterministic import analysis with file:line evidence. Models may draft names and intent, which stay unverified until a human accepts them.
decisions.consequences: Every finding is reproducible and cites evidence. Languages without import analysis get structural coverage only.

decisions.title: A dependency-free, dual-era MCP server
decisions.context: MCP 2026-07-28 is stateless with server/discover, while most clients still speak 2025-11-25 with an initialize handshake. The CLI ships as one bundled file.
decisions.decision: Implement JSON-RPC over stdio directly, supporting both the legacy initialize lifecycle and modern per-request _meta with server/discover.
decisions.consequences: No SDK dependency to track; protocol changes must be followed by hand.

decisions.title: The contract lives in the repository
decisions.context: Documentation is used when it lives where the work happens, and hand-made diagrams rot when they live elsewhere.
decisions.decision: The blueprint is a plain JSON file in the repository, versioned with the code. The browser edits it through the File System Access API or exports it; nothing depends on a hosted service.
decisions.consequences: Blueprint changes go through normal code review. Canvas layout is kept in a separate file so contract diffs stay clean.

decisions.title: Remove the classic map workspace
decisions.context: ADR-001 made the map canvas secondary. The Studio now covers opening a repository or folder, the live system design and editing the contract, while the classic map (repository-to-diagram analysis, file explorer and viewer, evidence inspector, chat agent, project store and export) duplicated surface area, dependencies and security boundary for a product Rassam no longer is.
decisions.decision: Delete the /map route and everything only it used: the workbench shell and UI, the chat agent, the deterministic map analyzer and its AI enrichment, the local project store and export format, and the /api/chat, /api/files, /api/repo and /api/source-grant routes. The product is the Studio, the engine, the CLI and MCP server, and the settings page.
decisions.consequences: The components workbench-shell, workbench-ui, chat-agent and analysis leave the contract; local-store shrinks to saved model settings. Projects saved by the classic map stay in the browser's storage but are no longer read. Model access remains only for the optional "tell Rassam what to change" path.
